data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmForeignKeyRebuildRisk
data.value: Note: the primary key referenced by {0} foreign key(s) changes, and the referenced column may no longer be a candidate key. If so, recreating the foreign key (on SQLite, the foreign key check after the sync) fails; on MySQL / Oracle the change may be left partially applied (the foreign key gone while the primary key is already changed).

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmUniqueConstraintDropRisk
data.value: Note: the unique constraint(s) below cover a column that an existing foreign key references. Dropping them removes the candidate key, so the drop may be rejected or the foreign key may break (unless the primary key still covers the same column): {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmForeignKeyTypeMismatch
data.value: Note: the foreign keys below would end up with different types on their two ends, so they are NOT dropped and re-added, and a selected addition or recreate of them is left out. A column change that the database refuses while such a foreign key is in place will fail (the database stays unchanged). Change the column on both ends to the same type: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmDescriptionCharactersReplaced
data.value: Note: the descriptions below contain characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (such as emoji). This database cannot store them and saves each one as "?": {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmUniqueConstraintDroppedWithColumn
data.value: Note: the unique constraints below are dropped because a column they use is dropped, even though dropping them is not selected. They are not re-created; add a unique constraint on the remaining columns if you need one: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmUniqueConstraintReplacedByPrimaryKey
data.value: Note: the unique constraints below are dropped because the primary key is moved onto the same columns, even though dropping them is not selected. This database cannot keep a unique constraint and a primary key on the same columns; the primary key keeps the values unique: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmSelectedItemRequiresUnselected
data.value: Note: the selected changes below are skipped because they need a change you did not select (a new table or column, a primary key change, or dropping a constraint in the database; shown in parentheses). Select that change too to apply them: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmTableLeftWithoutColumns
data.value: Note: the column drops below are skipped because they would leave the table without any column. A database table needs at least one column. To remove the table, delete it from the diagram and select dropping the table: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmTableWithoutColumns
data.value: Note: the tables below are not created because they have no columns in the diagram. A database table needs at least one column. Add columns to them in the diagram, then sync again: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmTableRebuildLosesImportDiscardedContent
data.value: Note: the changes to the tables below are skipped. This database applies them by rebuilding the table, and the rebuilt table would silently lose what the import could not bring into the diagram (listed after each table), together with its data. To sync these tables, first fix in the database what the import dropped (for example, rename a column whose name differs from another only in case or surrounding spaces, or drop a foreign key to a table outside the import), then import again: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmUniqueConstraintRebuildKeptForForeignKey
data.value: Note: the column changes of the unique constraints below are skipped, and each stays in its old form. The sync drops every key that the foreign key shown after the constraint relies on, and re-creates two or more of them, so whatever the order, the database would refuse the last drop after the earlier re-created key was gone, leaving that key dropped. The unique constraint kept in its old form keeps supporting the foreign key, so the other changes still run. To change its columns, run the sync again after this one (table / constraint (foreign key)): {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmTableChangeBreaksDependentView
data.value: Note: for the tables below, dropping the table and adding or removing columns are skipped; the other changes still run. Views in the database (listed after each table) read these tables, and these changes would leave the views unreadable, so the sync would be rolled back. To sync these changes, first change or drop the views in the database, then import again: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmTableChangeBreaksDependentTrigger
data.value: Note: for the tables below, dropping the table and adding or removing columns are skipped; the other changes still run. Triggers in the database (listed after each table) refer to these tables or their columns, and these changes would make the triggers fail when they fire, so the sync would be rolled back. To sync these changes, first change or drop the triggers in the database, then import again: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmForeignKeyNotOnCandidateKey
data.value: Note: the referenced columns of the foreign keys below are not exactly a primary key or a unique constraint after the sync. Adding them is likely to fail; on MySQL / Oracle, recreating an existing one can leave it dropped: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmConstraintRebuildAroundEmptyColumnChange
data.value: Note: the constraints below are dropped before a column change that this database accepts only while the column has no values (a change of the type kind, or a lower precision or scale; old type → new type), and re-added after it unless the sync removes them. If the column has data, the change fails, and because DDL is not rolled back, the dropped constraints stay dropped: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmConstraintRebuildAroundRowDependentChange
data.value: Note: the constraints below are dropped before a statement that the rows already in the database can refuse (a new primary key or unique constraint on columns with duplicate or empty values, NOT NULL on a column that holds NULL, a shorter type than the values, a NOT NULL column added to a table that has rows, or a change to a column a computed column may use), and re-added after it unless the sync removes them. If the database refuses that statement, the sync stops there, and because DDL is not rolled back, the dropped constraints stay dropped: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmDefaultOnColumnTypeKindChange
data.value: Note: the columns below have a default value in the database and their type changes kind (old type → new type). The sync keeps the database's default; if it does not fit the new type, the sync or a later insert that uses the default fails (when the sync fails on MySQL or Oracle, DDL is not rolled back and the statements before it stay applied): {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmSchemaQualifiedTableName
data.value: Note: the tables below have a dot in their name. SQLite reads such a name as a table in an attached database (the part before the dot), so the sync fails unless that database is attached: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmSetDefaultOnNotNullColumn
data.value: Note: the foreign keys below use SET DEFAULT on NOT NULL referencing columns (in parentheses). SQL Server creates them only when those columns have a DEFAULT constraint in the database; the diagram does not carry defaults, so they fail (error 1762) unless the columns already have one: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmSetNullOnNotNullColumn
data.value: Note: the referencing columns (in parentheses) of the SET NULL foreign keys below are NOT NULL after the sync. The foreign keys are created, but deleting or updating a referenced parent row fails because the columns cannot be set to NULL. Make the columns nullable or change the referential action: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmSetNullOnNotNullColumnExcluded
data.value: Note: the referencing columns (in parentheses) of the SET NULL foreign keys below are NOT NULL after the sync. This database cannot create such a foreign key, so the plan leaves out the additions and recreations you selected, and does not drop and re-add a foreign key already in the database. A column change that the database refuses then fails, and if the change goes through, deleting or updating a referenced parent row fails. Make the columns nullable or change the referential action: {0}

data.name: SchemaSync_ExecuteConfirmRebuildDropsAttributes
data.value: Note: rebuilding a table recreates it from the diagram, which does not model column attributes such as default values or CHECK constraints, constraint clauses, or table options such as WITHOUT ROWID. The attributes below exist in the database today and will NOT be reproduced (indexes and triggers are preserved): {0}
